findings.title: Full-size badge covers the cooldown countdown on abilities with no hotkey
findings.detail: When command.hotKey is null the badge goes at button.y + 2f. Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI draws the cooldown text centred at rect.y, padded by 8px each side, so a countdown like '12.3 secs' spans roughly x+8 to x+67 of the 75px button at y to y+LineHeight. The badge (x+3, width text+4) overlaps it, and because it is drawn in a postfix it sits on top of the countdown. hotKey comes from ability.def.hotKey (Command_Ability.cs:60), which many abilities leave unset. Fix at one place: when hotKey is null and ability.CooldownTicksRemaining > 0 (or always), put the badge at button.y + 3f + Text.LineHeight, the same row as when a hotkey is set, so it always sits below the top text line.

findings.title: Limiting the width does not stop a long translation spilling out: the label wraps
findings.detail: Verse's label styles have word wrap on, so a translation wider than button.width - 8 wraps onto a second line inside a rect that is only one line (size.y) tall, and that line draws over the icon or off the box. Cutting the text short makes it stay inside the box: use text.Truncate(r.width - 2f) when you call Widgets.Label.

findings.title: Full-size badge starts 1px into the hotkey line
findings.detail: Vanilla draws the hotkey at butRect.y + 3f with height Text.LineHeight (Tiny), so it ends at y+3+LH. The badge starts at y+2+LH and its gray background covers the bottom pixel of the hotkey text. Use + 3f to match vanilla's vector.y.

findings.title: Steam Deck: the A-button icon is 21px tall, so the badge with no hotkey overlaps it
findings.detail: In Steam Deck non-keyboard mode the first gizmo draws a 21x21 ButtonA texture at the hotkey position whatever hotKey is set to. A badge at y+2 (no hotkey) or y+2+LineHeight (about 18px) still overlaps it on that one gizmo. This is minor and only affects the first gizmo.

checked: verify_patches: all 4 targets in AbilityAIAutocast.cs bind (Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI prefix/postfix, Command.GizmoOnGUIShrunk prefix/postfix)
The badge rect uses GetWidth(maxWidth) x 75, the same rect vanilla's Command_Ability.GizmoOnGUI uses for the button and cooldown bar

Shrunk placement: GizmoOnGUIShrunk passes a size x size rect with parms.shrunk; vanilla draws no top-right label, bottom label or cooldown when shrunk, and the hotkey is drawn at y+0, so bottom-left …
Text.LineHeight is read after Text.Font = Tiny, so the hotkey offset uses the same line height vanilla uses for the hotkey
Charges (TopRightLabel) are drawn on the right edge at y+3 and do not collide with a left-edge badge of normal length
GUI.color and Text.Font are set back to white/Small after drawing, matching what vanilla's GizmoOnGUIInt leaves behind
The badge is drawn only on Repaint, so it adds no layout or input handling
